records.reason: Direct OSCE baseline on constitutional changes and the incumbent-benefiting electoral framework; strong, in-period background for 2022 political freedom.
Useful context on the constrained observation environment, but it is a press-release level summary rather than substantive findings.
Older wire recap of the same constitutional term-reset baseline already captured more directly by E0058; adds no material 2022-specific detail.
Later retrospective synthesis that is useful for interpretation, but it is not contemporaneous with the target year.
Direct contemporaneous evidence of censorship and protest suppression through state media controls; strong target-year record.
Broader contemporaneous escalation with media blocking and large-scale arrests; distinct enough to keep as one of the best illustrative incidents.
Early anti-war detention report that repeats the same protest-repression mechanism already established by stronger retained synthesis records.
Another protest-treatment report on the same crackdown; it does not add a materially new mechanism beyond the retained evidence.
Secondary AP account of the same fake-news and protest-charging crackdown; redundant once the stronger direct reports are retained.
Strong year-end synthesis with counts across arrests, criminal cases, blocking, and treason sentences; high-value independent summary.
Useful corroboration and mechanism detail from the same monitoring family, but largely overlaps the retained year-end synthesis.
Direct closure of Amnesty’s Moscow office and related blocking actions, which is a distinct civil-society suppression example.
Another protest and journalist-silencing account that repeats the already retained repression pattern without adding a distinct mechanism.
Independent UN-level corroboration of harassment, detentions, and mass arrests tied to journalists and peaceful demonstrators.
Strong retrospective synthesis on repression, censorship, and political prisoners in 2022; high-value annual summary.
Corroborative retrospective detail with annual case counts, but it overlaps the retained Memorial synthesis.
Direct in-period law expanding LGBT propaganda restrictions; a separate rights-restriction mechanism from protest and media repression.
Current RSF summary is useful broad corroboration of the post-2022 media environment, but it is not a 2022-dated primary record.
Annual country chapter summarizing 2022 war-censorship laws and suppression of dissent; strong synthesis evidence.
Methodology-only page that helps assess the reliability of the OVD-Info family, but it is not direct conduct evidence.
Background mission index that supports the observation-coverage context, but it is not a substantive findings document.
Direct OSCE statement on the illegal annexation and its human-rights implications, squarely in period.
Contemporaneous Amnesty report on coercive sham referenda and occupation-control tactics; strong annexation-related evidence.
Official U.S. reporting on the legal extension of Russian rule, citizenship coercion, martial law, and restrictions in occupied areas.
Independent Freedom House corroboration on coercive citizenship and deportation practices in occupied Crimea.
Direct evidence of state propaganda and sanctions for dissent through the Education Ministry, a distinct civic-space mechanism.

remaining_concerns: The strongest evidence clusters around censorship, protest repression, and occupation-control measures; there is less direct evidence here on broader administrative governance outside those mechanisms.
Several usable records are retrospective syntheses or methodology/context pages, so the chapter still depends on a mix of direct contemporaneous reports and later summaries.
A few incident-level protest reports were dropped as repetitive after stronger annual or institutional syntheses were retained.
